q: Subject-verb agreement: The boys ____ playing football in the field. (P4)
explain: Plural subject 'boys' takes the plural auxiliary verb 'are'.

q: Subject-verb agreement: Every student ____ a textbook. (P4)
explain: 'Every student' is singular and takes the singular verb 'has'.

q: Collective noun: A ____ of lions was resting under the acacia tree. (P4)
explain: The group term for lions is a 'pride'.
hint: Think of a pride of magnificent lions.

q: Collective noun: A ____ of wolves hunted across the valley. (P4)
explain: A group of wolves is called a 'pack'.
hint: A team of hunting wolves is a pack.

q: Collective noun: A ____ of bees flew around the hive. (P4)
explain: A large group of flying insects like bees is a 'swarm'.

q: Collective noun: A ____ of cattle grazed in the pasture. (P4)
explain: A group of grazing mammals is a 'herd'.
hint: Group name for cows or elephants.

q: Prefixes: Adding 'un-' to 'happy' creates 'unhappy', which means ____. (P4)
explain: The prefix 'un-' means 'not' or the reverse.

q: Suffixes: Adding '-ful' to 'care' produces 'careful', which means ____. (P4)
explain: The suffix '-ful' means 'full of' or characterized by.

q: Choose the correctly punctuated direct speech sentence: (P4)
explain: Direct speech requires a comma before the opening quotation marks.
hint: Comma before speech marks and closing quotes after punctuation.

q: Possessive apostrophe: This is the ____ bag (belonging to one teacher). (P4)
explain: Singular possession adds apostrophe-s ('s).

q: Possessive apostrophe: The ____ dormitory was clean (belonging to many girls). (P4)
explain: Plural regular nouns ending in -s take only an apostrophe after the s.
hint: For plural ending in 's', add only the apostrophe at the end.
